# Hooks and plugins

Verified 2026-10-28 against the official [hook reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) and [plugin overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins). Use the installed host's schema when adding features beyond this bundled example.

## Project hooks

Configure project lifecycle hooks in `.claude/settings.json`. Events such as `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` contain matcher groups and command handlers. Hook handlers receive JSON on stdin; do not assume tool arguments appear in invented shell environment variables.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [
          {"type": "command", "command": "node .claude/hooks/check.cjs"}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The script path above is an example: create the handler before enabling it. It must resolve paths correctly from the session working directory. AgentKit instead installs its actual cross-platform launcher and adapter in `.agentkit/hooks/`, merged into project settings.

Parse the payload's event, tool and input fields. Use the documented output schema for context or decisions. Advisory checks should not block a build because a payload is unfamiliar; enforce a restriction only when the requested policy requires it. Test success, failure and malformed input with synthetic payloads. Never log credentials from tool arguments.

Inspect hooks using the host UI. If they do not run, check project trust, settings loading, event/matcher names, Node availability and the actual handler path. Do not disable user protections or change global trust as a troubleshooting shortcut.

## Plugins

Plugins package components such as skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers. Use `/plugin` to inspect the installed host's management UI; verify a plugin's source, permissions and dependencies before installing it. AgentKit's project installer is usable without publishing or installing a host plugin.

When authoring a plugin, follow the current official manifest/component documentation rather than inventing `init`, `publish` or package-registry commands. Keep project source edits separate from user-wide configuration. Publishing is a distinct authorized action, not part of testing a local plugin.
